result:
All five defects fixed and verified against the PDFs before editing. Every one was real.

**[1.1] major — the false "only other mention of power" clause.** Confirmed. `grep -i power` returns eleven lines (footnote 1, §2.2, §2.2.1, the §3.3 fix, §5 twice, a reference title); my round-1 pattern `energy|watt|power consum|joule` matched exactly one. That's the R9 failure mode the brief warns about, and I committed it while writing an R9-motivated critique. The load-bearing claim survives — power is never *measured* — so the sentence now says power "runs through the paper as a design pressure without ever being measured — no power figure, axis or table," which is what I can defend.

**[1.4] was worse than reported.** Checking it showed I had the direction wrong on *both* halves, not just the sched_ext half. §3.5 says "The takeaway is that new scheduler designs come and go" — so CFS being replaced by EEVDF is the paper's prediction *coming true*, not a contradiction of it. And §5 explicitly proposes "a scheduler that is a collection of modules: the core module and optimization modules," which sched_ext vindicates. The paragraph now reads as vindication of both, with the sched_ext match softened as asked.

**[1.5], [1.2], [1.3]** confirmed and corrected: Table 4 puts Overload-on-Wakeup last at 22% (it leads only on the database workload); the "less than 150 lines" sentence sits in §4.2 and covers the visualiser alone; the worked example is in §9, not §8 — which `evidence.md` had right and the answer had wrong.

I left everything else untouched, per the instruction not to rewrite passing work.

Two things worth flagging:

- **Paper 2 grew 492 → 529 words** (17.6% over the 450 target, inside the 25% threshold but up from 9%). Separating vindication from contradiction and qualifying sched_ext genuinely costs more words than the incorrect one-liner. I recovered ~20 by merging sentences in the Table 4 paragraph, then stopped rather than cut substance the validator had passed.
- Reference [3]'s URL was overrunning the right margin by 75pt. Fixed with `\allowbreak` at the slashes — the document now compiles with **zero overfull boxes**, still requiring no packages.

`evidence.md` was corrected at the five corresponding rows, including the bad grep pattern itself, so the audit trail no longer vouches for the error. `submission.md` has a round-2 section, and I added a new "least confident" item 0 about the grep-discipline failure: the defect was a search error, not a reading error — I built a critique on a pattern narrow enough to confirm what I expected. I re-checked my two other "the paper is silent about X" claims on that basis; both hold.

Lint OK, R5 clean, 3 pages, bare-`article` compile OK.
